commonErrors.example: A learner writes on the worksheet that energy keeps cycling round an ecosystem forever, coming back to the producers.

fixIt.corrected: Energy flows one way, sunlight in and heat out; what cycles is matter, carbon included, not energy.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: say in one sentence what happens to the energy dot in scene s6 and what happens to the carbon dot.

commonErrors.misconception: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem.

commonErrors.example: On the exit ticket, a learner picks the statement that energy is recycled through the ecosystem.

fixIt.corrected: Energy enters as sunlight and leaves as heat, never returning: the dot that loops round and round is carbon, not energy.
fixIt.prompt: Fix it: explain in one sentence what the red energy dot does after the sun is replaced by the moon in scene s6.

commonErrors.misconception: Energy is recycled through the ecosystem.

modelAnswers.answer: Most energy is lost as heat from respiration, in egestion and excretion, and in uneaten or undigested parts, so only about a tenth is built into new tissue that the next level can eat.
modelAnswers.question: Explain why only about 10% of the energy at one trophic level reaches the next level, and what happens to the rest.

modelAnswers.answer: Energy flows one way: sunlight in, heat out. Carbon cycles: photosynthesis draws CO2 into plants, while respiration, combustion and decomposition return CO2 to the air.
modelAnswers.question: Compare how energy and carbon move through an ecosystem: state which one cycles and which flows one way, naming the processes involved.

nextSteps: Reteach the energy-recycling trap from the paired notes trap before any further ecology work: energy flows one way, sunlight in and heat out, while matter cycles.
Practise the 10% rule from scene s3, working the 20 000 kJ ticket example level by level before the next lesson.
strengths: Most of the class can state the 10% rule: only about a tenth of the energy at one level reaches the next.
The class can tell energy flow apart from the carbon cycle, naming photosynthesis, respiration and combustion.
